# S53 — Argument-parser failures bypass JSON error envelopes

**Findings:** S46 planning; slicer edit --json prints argparse usage only · **Size: S** · **Tree:** cli

**Not in this slice:** changing command semantics or accepting invalid arguments.

## Why

`slicer edit --json` with missing required arguments exits 2 with argparse usage on stderr and no JSON on stdout. cli.main calls parse_args before its SlicerError handler. Agents cannot use the documented error envelope for parser failures.

## Files

src/slicer/cli.py; tests/test_errors.py; docs/agents.md.

## Failing tests

Missing required arguments, unknown options, invalid choices and conflicting parser options produce a usage envelope when --json is requested. Human errors and --help still work.

## Implement

Use an ArgumentParser subclass that raises a private parser-error exception, including nested subparsers. Handle parsing in main with a shared root namespace for recognized top-level command attribution. On parser failure, exact --json before the first -- requests one usage envelope on stdout, including misplaced flags, without accepting invalid syntax. Preserve argparse usage and diagnostic on stderr; return 2. Unknown/unrecognized commands use null attribution; nested prose failures use prose. Reuse envelope formatting and preserve runtime errors, successful parsing and help behavior.

## Check

Test missing arguments/values, unknown options/commands, invalid choices/integers, conflicting remove modes, nested prose, misplaced --json and tokens after --. Exercise main(argv) and python3 -m slicer; assert status, envelope, stderr, help behavior and no handlers/state mutations. Run focused and full unittest suites, slicer check and git diff --check. Normal test temporary directories are authorized for this session.

## Git

Review the complete diff, mark done only after validation, commit as S53: return JSON envelopes for argument-parser failures, then push main to origin/main as authorized. Never force-push.
